beats.text: Stand at the edge of a high cliff and you feel two fears, not one.
The fear of falling — and something stranger: the pull of the thought that you could simply jump.
Kierkegaard said that second feeling is the whole human condition in miniature.
He called anxiety the dizziness of freedom — the vertigo of knowing you could choose anything.
Animals have no such dread. Only a creature that is free can be terrified of its own possibility.
You cannot reason your way across the gap. At some point you must leap — and commit before you are sure.
So the anxiety never fully leaves. It is the price of being free.

attribution: Søren Kierkegaard · The Concept of Anxiety
